nodes.label: Problem: search ranks, it never verifies
nodes.rationale: Ranking is a popularity guess; a search engine never checks whether a sentence is true. The factory decomposes a question, researches in parallel, then re-checks every claim against the page it came from and stores the supporting passage so the report says 'here, check me'.

nodes.label: retrieval-service (port 8081)
nodes.rationale: The only built-and-working service; also the single quota boundary so all web access, credits and caching are counted in exactly one place.

nodes.label: control-plane (port 8083, blueprint)
nodes.rationale: The only service that connects to Postgres; it will own restart-proof fan-in state.

nodes.label: common module (empty toolbox)
nodes.rationale: Exists so a shared Claim/ResearchFinding type makes a field mismatch a compile error rather than a production mystery; zero source files today. Must never get spring-boot-maven-plugin, which would repackage it and break it as a library jar.

nodes.label: Maven multi-module aggregator build
nodes.rationale: Root pom is packaging=pom, holds no code, and imports the Spring Boot BOM so children ask for libraries without naming versions.

nodes.label: Suspicious: java.version never wired to the compiler
nodes.rationale: Only retrieval-service sets maven.compiler.release; agent-service and control-plane declare java.version but never connect it, so the first record written in them may fail with 'records are not supported in -source 8'. The same trap already bit retrieval-service in Session 4.

nodes.label: Spring Boot 4.1.0 + embedded Tomcat
nodes.rationale: Three boot behaviours matter: component scan, auto-configuration from the classpath, and an embedded Tomcat so the built program IS the server with no deploy step.

nodes.label: Jackson 3 (tools.jackson.*)
nodes.rationale: Works invisibly for @RequestBody and responses, and explicitly for the two Redis payloads. Jackson 3 renames packages from com.fasterxml.jackson to tools.jackson, so pasted internet snippets will not compile, and its parse/write failures are unchecked so no try/catch is forced.

nodes.label: Records, not Lombok
nodes.rationale: Every data shape is an immutable record; plain Java now generates the constructor, accessors, equals and hashCode, so the Lombok dependency is deliberately refused.

nodes.label: Two RestClient beans and @Qualifier ambiguity
nodes.rationale: Adding a second bean of type RestClient retroactively breaks the existing injection point, so both consumers must name their bean on the constructor parameter. The failure is at startup, loudly, not at first use.

nodes.label: Redis 7 (Lettuce client)
nodes.rationale: Two jobs only: the 24h search cache and the daily credit counter. Lettuce connects lazily, so a dead Redis lets the app boot fine and then fails the first request with a 500 - Redis is on the critical path, not an optional speed-up.

nodes.label: Redis allkeys-lru eviction with 256MB cap
nodes.rationale: Redis defaults to noeviction, which refuses new writes when full - wrong for a cache where every entry is disposable and re-fetchable. No volume is configured, which is acceptable for a cache and a daily counter.

nodes.label: SearXNG metasearch container
nodes.rationale: The only path to the open web for search. Exactly one setting is changed: json added to search.formats, without which SearXNG returns HTML meant for human eyes and the JSON parser chokes - a documented trap that already cost this project time.

nodes.label: Python extractor sidecar
nodes.rationale: Written in Python because trafilatura, the best boilerplate-stripping library, is a Python library. It never fetches URLs, so it physically cannot report UNREACHABLE, ROBOTS_DENIED or TOO_LARGE - those belong to Java at fetch time.

nodes.label: Docker + docker-compose (5 containers)
nodes.rationale: Port mapping, healthchecks and build-vs-pull are the three details that matter. The three Java services are deliberately NOT in the compose file - they run on the host and reach the containers over localhost.

nodes.label: Postgres 16 + pgvector, Flyway, Hibernate validate
nodes.rationale: pgvector is chosen now so nobody has to migrate later. ddl-auto=validate means never let Hibernate change the schema; the rule is migration first, entity second. All three tables exist and are empty.

nodes.label: Redpanda (Kafka-compatible broker)
nodes.rationale: Kafka is chosen for the orchestrator-to-researcher hops precisely because subtasks run 5-90s with high variance and a durable drop box tolerates that where a request/reply call does not. Today no Java code touches Kafka at all - no spring-kafka in any pom.

nodes.label: Actuator /actuator/health
nodes.rationale: Declared in all three services, but nothing automated calls it - the Java services are not in docker-compose, so it is checked by a human or the IDE dashboard. Week 5's Kubernetes plan needs exactly this probe back.

nodes.label: Test stack: JUnit 6 resolved, Mockito unused
nodes.rationale: 17 tests across four files in retrieval-service. contextLoads looks pointless but is a wiring smoke test: @SpringBootTest boots the whole context, so it only passes if every bean was built and disambiguated. Testcontainers is the stated convention but is not in place, which is why the suite fails when Docker is down.

nodes.label: Suspicious: common/README claims a dependency nothing declares
nodes.rationale: common/README says the three services declare it as a dependency; reading all four poms shows no such dependency anywhere. Intent is not wiring.

nodes.label: RetrievalController (the doorman)
nodes.rationale: Every method is one line; it knows HTTP, JSON and status codes and deliberately knows nothing about caching, credits, tiers or search engines.

nodes.label: SearchService (the librarian)
nodes.rationale: Knows caching, credits, tiers and search engines and deliberately knows nothing about HTTP, so a future in-process caller could use it directly with no HTTP anywhere.

nodes.label: QuotaService (the meter reader)
nodes.rationale: He reads the meter; he does not switch off the power.

nodes.label: SourceTierResolver (the quality grader)
nodes.rationale: Lower is better: government 1, big press 2, unknown 3, blog-patterns 4. Lists live in YAML so adding a trusted site is a one-line text edit plus a restart, no Java touched.

nodes.label: UrlNormalizer (the alias detective)
nodes.rationale: Four different-looking addresses can point at one article; without canonicalization one article gets filed under four names and fetched four times. It deliberately never strips a param merely for looking unimportant - ?page=1 and ?page=2 stay distinct.

nodes.label: ExtractCacheKey (the label maker)
nodes.rationale: extract:v1: plus 16 hex chars. The v1 is deliberate: to invalidate every cached page at once you bump it to v2 rather than hunting down and deleting keys.

nodes.label: Hashing (the fingerprint clerk)
nodes.rationale: Deliberately lifted out of SearchService once a second class needed it, so the two cache-key recipes cannot silently drift apart. It is the one part of the extract chain that is not idle.

nodes.label: ExtractorClient (the unemployed courier)
nodes.rationale: Built correctly, registered as a bean, and called by absolutely nobody - the canonical example of 'wired but never called'.

nodes.label: Suspicious: the quota is a fuel gauge, not a fuel cutoff
nodes.rationale: SearchService.search calls recordSpend on every miss but never asks remaining() first, and remaining() floors at zero, so once out of credits it calmly reports 0 forever while searches keep going. Scoped, not forgotten: real gates arrive in Week 5.

nodes.label: Blueprint props (built, unused)
nodes.rationale: Three empty Postgres tables, three Redpanda topics with no producer, an empty common module, and a courier plus a specialist with no work order between them.
